messages.subject: DAGAR model in 'rgeneric'
parts:
Dear all, 
I am trying to fit a DAGAR model (Datta et al., 2019) for Spatial Disease Mapping in R-INLA.
I am trying to use the 'rgeneric' function but I came across some questions.

  • The model proposes that the random effect('w') of region i, defined as: 

where e_i are independent and N(0, t_i) distributed.

N(i) includes all the neighbours less than i

bij denotes the autoregressive model  
 
The precision matrix ('Q') is define as: Q=t(L)FL
Where:
t() is transpose,
'L' can be re writen as L=I-B
 'I' is the identity matrix of size n (n=total number of areas)
 'B' is a lowe triangular matrix that holds the values of bij
'F' is a diagonal matrix with t_i in the diagonal
 
The model also state that: 

 

 
My question is: 
  • Can this be model fit using a formulated model in R-INLA?
  • In the 'rgeneric' definition the 'graph' function works just with the upper triangular matrix, is this an issue since the model emphasize the uses of the lower inferior matrix?
  • For the 'Q() function' is it possible to define it as:
Q <- function() {
  
  param <- interpret.theta()
  #param$rho
  #param$prec
  
  I<-diag(x=1, 44)
 
  for (i in 1:44) {
    for (j in 1:44){
      B[i,j]<-param$rho/(1+(n[i]-1)*param$rho^2)
  }}
  F<-diag(x=c(mvrnorm(n=44, mu=0, Sigma=param$prec)), 44)
  
  return(t(I-B)F(I-B))
}
 
Thank you very much in advance.

--
Diego


Datta, Abhirup, Sudipto Banerjee, James S. Hodges, and Leiwen Gao. "Spatial disease mapping using directed acyclic graph auto-regressive (DAGAR) models." Bayesian Analysis (2018).

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] DAGAR model in 'rgeneric'
parts:
All Gaussian model components can be represented in rgeneric.

in your case, you'll have two 'graphs', one that is for the precision
matrix, and one for L.

the rgeneric defines Q (precision matrix), so you have to compute that
one from their representation. its like LL', depending on how you
define L.

just make sure you define L to be a sparse matrix, so that L %*% t(L)
is sparse as well.

you can use Q to define the graph, unless some of its elements is zero
that is later non-zero.

H
